raw_response:
I farm only 4.1 mu, so I cannot take big risks. What feeds my family and brings cash is still the wheat-maize rotation, same as around here. I did not study books, so I go by what I saw on my own land and what the other households do. If wheat comes up weak, I lose twice, because then the maize is also delayed. So for wheat I will still sow in early October, use the seed we can get easily in town, put a fair base fertilizer, and save a little money for one topdressing and a few irrigations if the weather is dry. I cannot spend too much at once because people in the family work outside and cash must stay in hand, but I also do not dare cut fertilizer too hard. After wheat harvest in June, I will rush to plant maize right away, with simple tillage, not too much delay. For maize I will use hybrid seed, a bit less fertilizer than wheat, and irrigate only if there is no rain, because pumping water costs money. I do things the steady way, not chasing the highest yield, just trying to keep both crops safe.
